parsed.why: Cross-dressing offence struck down, 72% acceptance and decriminalisation backing, but police extortion via residual clauses, a magistrate's courtroom exclusion of a trans woman, and 69 documented violence cases with state inaction.

No criminalisation and courts granting remedies, but a trans foreign national held in a male centre with HRT cut three months, no hate-crime protection, official hostility and residual anti-LGBT acts.

Progressive recognition law, X markers and identity-based hospital placement, but a record hate-crime year, government decrees on trans prison housing, and activists documenting deteriorating safety despite the framework.

Criminalisation enforced by arrest on clothing and appearance, routine police extortion, trans women jailed in male prisons facing sexual violence, an active moral-police unit, and a hostile society with no recourse.

Court decriminalisation plus a constitutional reading covering gender identity, no trans-specific offence or documented targeting; thin record with no statutory protections and unresolved custody and border practice.
